questions: Are we allowed to have S_i values that exceed typical integer bounds (e.g., larger than 64-bit) as long as we compute modulo 998244353 at the end, or must each S_i fit within standard integer types during intermediate calculations?
Is the sequence S considered ordered, i.e., are sequences with the same multiset of elements but different permutations counted separately if they satisfy the conditions?

For the gcd condition, is it required that gcd(S_1, ..., S_N) = 1 exactly, or is it sufficient that no common divisor >1 exists? (The phrasing suggests exactly 1, but could be interpreted as 'no common divisor >1'.)
Can S_i be 1, or must they be strictly greater than 0? (The prompt says positive integers, which includes 1.)

Is the product of all elements computed as the exact integer product before taking modulo, or can we take modulo during multiplication? (The modulo instruction applies to the sum of scores, not necessarily each product.)
Are there any constraints on the magnitude of S_i beyond being positive integers? For example, could they be arbitrarily large as long as they satisfy the equations?

Does the condition f(S_i/S_{i+1}) = A_i require that S_i and S_{i+1} are coprime when expressed as a fraction, or does f automatically use the reduced form? (The definition of f uses coprime P and Q, so it's automatic.)
If multiple good sequences exist, is the sum of their scores taken over all possible sequences, including those with different lengths? (N is fixed, so length is N.)
